whatItIs.text: A summer squash picked young — soft seeds, edible skin — known as courgette in Britain and France; in botany its fruit is technically a berry.

historyNote.text: Squashes were domesticated in Mexico and Central America over 7,000 years ago, but the zucchini itself was bred in Milan in the late 19th century — first described in a Milanese publication in 1901 — and reached America with Italian immigrants in the early 1920s.

howToChoose.text: Choose small, firm, glossy squash about 15-20 cm long; flowers still attached signal real freshness. Bitterness in any cucurbit means stop eating — discard rather than taste more.

storage.text: Refrigerate loose in the crisper, unwashed until use. The rulebook has the window.

foodSafetyRef.note: fresh-vegetable windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Soft zucchini grates into fritters, bakes into bread, or melts into pasta sauces and ratatouille; over-large ones peel, seed, and roast or stuff.
